events.behavior: The determinant-948 rank-17 MW lattice and its 1311 height-4 pairs entered the repository.
events.method: Recover the Gram matrix and mine additive motifs, cliques, and saturation data among short vectors.
events.meaning: The endpoint became an exact positive lattice constraint, but not yet an equation or a source construction.
events.generalization: Treat a large MW basis as a lattice fingerprint first; search for simpler fibrations before solving for all sections.
events.status: exact computation

events.behavior: The 167-variable three-hub and 48-variable rank-3 motif systems timed out; small residuals did not provide sections.
events.method: Export sliced polynomial section systems to msolve over GF(101).
events.meaning: The direct equation representation discarded too little structure and was computationally wrong-sized.
events.generalization: Compress with exact group-law/lattice operations before Groebner elimination; timeout is an experiment, not an obstruction theorem.
events.status: negative experiment

events.behavior: The determinant-948 transcendental lattice was matched to the (D,N)=(6,79) Eichler order and CM vectors of discriminants -3 and -24.
events.method: Even ternary-form filtering, exact quaternion/Eichler construction, Gross vectors, Atkin-Lehner orbits, and inverse-Clifford transport.
events.meaning: The recovered lattice was tied to Shimura arithmetic; the -3 vector cuts out the singular K3 with transcendental lattice A2.
events.generalization: Use discriminant forms, local ramification, and CM vectors to turn a lattice fingerprint into moduli coordinates and explicit boundary anchors.
events.status: exact computation

events.behavior: The explicit discriminant-3 K3 anchor was found; one E8 breaks to 2A2, producing E8+3A2/MW3, and an index-9 glue correction recovered regulator 316/9.
events.method: Embed the rank-19 NS as the orthogonal complement of a square -316 class and saturate the root-orthogonal section quotient.
events.meaning: Seventeen sections were exchanged for three sections plus root components; the missing factor 81 was a square of a saturation index, not a regulator contradiction.
events.generalization: Whenever regulator ratios are perfect squares, compute NS/(trivial+sections) before rejecting the model; glue is geometric data.
events.status: exact computation

events.behavior: A reverse q90,4,4 path changed rootless/MW17 into E6+2A3+2A1/MW3.
events.method: Enumerate primitive isotropic classes f=(a,b,v), split a new U integrally, classify child roots, and retain lower-MW frames.
events.meaning: MW rank disappeared only relative to the new fibration: the same rank-19 NS budget moved into reducible fibre roots.
events.generalization: Search the graph of primitive U embeddings, using root rank and equation cost as independent objectives.
events.status: exact path from bounded search

events.behavior: Finite-field A10/E6 section charts produced modular points and triangular reductions, but the split E6 chart and several seeds did not come from the transported fibration.
events.method: Tate coefficient gates, coordinate slicing, GCD scans with collision-factor saturation, finite-field enumeration, and Hensel probes.
events.meaning: An abstract ADE/MW label does not fix a marked elliptic fibration or a rational equation chart.
events.generalization: Execute the neighbor geometrically and transport F,O,components,sections before normalizing an equation ansatz.
events.status: mixed exact reductions and superseded experiments

events.behavior: The all-IV j=0 deformation was obstructed by MW-rank parity; a mixed I3/IV non-isotrivial family replaced it.
events.method: Compare the order-three automorphism/parity constraint with Shioda-Tate and derive a family with nonconstant j.
events.meaning: The root lattice A2 does not determine Kodaira type IV versus I3; fibre realization controls automorphisms and rank parity.
events.generalization: Enumerate Kodaira realizations of an ADE root system and test monodromy/automorphism constraints before section solving.
events.status: exact obstruction and viable replacement family

events.behavior: The bounded q25,4,4,4 backtrack reached E6+D4+2A2+A1/MW2 and was later reconstructed over QQ.
events.method: Widened beam search, exact U-splits, component-glue recovery, exhaustive GF(23) chart, CRT, and Hensel reconstruction.
events.meaning: The endpoint can be represented by two sections and root rank 15, but this backtrack does not identify the level-474 source polarization.
events.generalization: Minimize symbolic equation cost after lattice rank: number of sections, pole order, pair gates, and Weierstrass degree all matter.
events.status: exact path; explicit specialization has a Picard-rank-20 correction

events.behavior: Three E7+E8/MW2 Kumar frames were classified; H2 exposed q60 and q80 comparison fibrations, with Q80=E6+D5+A3/MW3.
events.method: Binary height forms, discriminant glue, exact neighbors, and bounded CM-stability scoring.
events.meaning: Q80 is a useful secondary polarization/compiler chart on the same lattice genus, not the source entrance.
events.generalization: Maintain a fibration atlas on one NS lattice; different polarizations should be scored for source meaning and compiler cost separately.
events.status: exact candidates from bounded search

events.behavior: The H3 q6 child E8+E6/MW3 and its degree-two rank-growing continuations were found at lattice/chamber level.
events.method: Exact neighbor enumeration, root adaptation, nef chamber reduction, and old-fibre-degree scoring.
events.meaning: A forward source-to-R17 corridor became available independently of the reverse low-MW ancestry.
events.generalization: A selected route is a certified path, not a shortest-path theorem; preserve alternatives and the search boundary.
events.status: exact retained path from bounded searches

events.behavior: The H21 intersection H92 component identified H3, not H2, as the level-474 source; the published genus-two model was normalized into the exact E7+E8/MW2 family.
events.method: Humbert intersection, modular solving, p-adic lifting, exact rational reconstruction, and comparison with the published rational point.
events.meaning: The construction direction changed from reverse discovery to forward execution from the actual QM/Kumar source.
events.generalization: Use moduli geometry to choose the source polarization; lattice isometry alone cannot tell which embedded U is historically or arithmetically canonical.
events.status: proved

events.behavior: The first q6 H3 neighbor was executed exactly, giving E8+E6/MW3.
events.method: Resolved Riemann-Roch pencil, binary quartic, Jacobian conversion, and fibre classification.
events.meaning: The lattice neighbor acquired an actual characteristic-zero equation and transported markings.
events.generalization: A neighbor certificate should have two layers: integral NS transport and an equation-level RR/Jacobian realization.
events.status: proved

events.behavior: Large q8 module ambients repeatedly appeared to have zero surviving kernels, generating bounded modular obstructions that were later superseded.
events.method: Principal-part matrices, local E7/E8 component modules, saturation probes, and multi-prime rank checks.
events.meaning: The computations were correct for the supplied wrongly marked/normalized modules but did not obstruct the true q8 divisor.
events.generalization: A full-rank obstruction is only as valid as its marking and module; pin the divisor identity and normalization before scaling linear algebra.
events.status: superseded bounded experiments

events.behavior: Reverse saturation exposed adapted coordinates such as x-m^2 and separated local component modules from global fibre twists; several apparent obstructions vanished or changed dimension.
events.method: One-uniformizer saturation, exact/two-prime kernel comparison, and resolved chart bases.
events.meaning: Cancellations belong to the saturated pushforward module, not to arbitrary monomial pole floors.
events.generalization: Compile local line-bundle modules by saturation and quotient conditions; never count exceptional components as independent scalar rows by default.
events.status: exact local modules plus superseded global interpretations

events.behavior: The generic Q80 low-q corridor reached a rootless/MW17 frame with every retained suffix divisor of old-fibre degree two.
events.method: Alternate-neighbor beam, chamber scoring, exact section/CVP walls, and stagewise integral transport.
events.meaning: A second complete lattice route demonstrated that the H3 selected path is not unique and supplied simpler compiler experiments.
events.generalization: Represent the field as a route graph, not one chain; retain multiple exact paths and optimize them by different costs.
events.status: proved lattice corridor

events.behavior: The Q80 specialization corridor was compiled over GF(73), showing repeated pole/intersection collapse and connected ADE quotient conditions.
events.method: Specialize actual divisors, saturate local modules, solve quotient-line conditions, compile quartics, and classify Jacobians.
events.meaning: At CM24, extra NS classes change roots, pole orders, and MW labels; specialized horizontals are regressions, not generic definitions.
events.generalization: Specialization is a typed operation with its own marking and Picard rank; recompute every divisor invariant after base change.
events.status: exact modular regression, later lifted to characteristic zero

events.behavior: Two bugs were isolated: the quartic covariant 2-cover was doubled again, and the q-normalizer omitted Dx. Collision degree fell 46 to 10; the exact 13-to-2 RR pencil produced D13/MW4.
events.method: Global height audit, direct rational-function residue derivation, two-prime regression, and exact QQ Jacobian certification.
events.meaning: The apparent high-degree obstruction came from a wrong group-law scale and a hidden vertical pole, not from the geometry.
events.generalization: Track isogeny/cover degree on every point map and clear complete rational expressions before CRT/local normalization.
events.status: proved correction and equation

events.behavior: The terminal Q80 CM24 q6 marking was recovered as a difference of easier exact sections, closing the exact QQ(sqrt(-3)) RR pencil and 4A2+A3+A5/MW2 child.
events.method: Replay unimodular transports, reconstruct high-incidence sections, identify a group-law difference modulo 73, then certify over characteristic zero.
events.meaning: A singular direct lift was bypassed without changing the selected divisor; generic rootless/MW17 remained distinct from the CM24 child.
events.generalization: When a marked section is singular to lift, construct a small exact MW basis and recover the target by group operations plus modular identification.
events.status: proved specialization equation

events.behavior: The D13 q24 orbit85 child and the complete D12-to-R17 degree-two lattice suffix were recovered; route-scout also showed valid but differently marked alternatives.

events.meaning: Matching ADE/MW sequences is insufficient: the selected D13/D12 marking determines whether the terminal rootless frame is pinned R17.
events.generalization: Every route edge must carry its full U embedding and forward/inverse transport, not just q and ADE labels.
events.status: proved lattice/marking path

events.behavior: The I9* resolution distinguished blow-up centres from twelve physical components; an ordinary-jet shortcut overcounted conditions, while the resolved component quotient left a two-plane.
events.method: Explicit blow-up graph, effective-cluster transport, smooth-collision quotient, and resolved valuation RR matrices.
events.meaning: Cancellation and dependence occur along connected exceptional geometry; centre counts are not component counts.
events.generalization: Build a physical component graph and valuation atlas before imposing local conditions; validate Euler/root data after compilation.
events.status: exact modular discovery, later lifted to QQ

events.behavior: Multi-prime reconstruction and structured Hensel lifting produced the exact q24 horizontal section over QQ.
events.method: Modular section sampling, CRT/rational reconstruction, structured Newton-Hensel lift, and literal equation substitution.
events.meaning: The selected lattice divisor acquired an exact rational horizontal representative.
events.generalization: Separate section reconstruction from the full RR lift; checkpoint exact identities so expensive local geometry need not be repeated.

events.behavior: The characteristic-zero resolved RR lift compiled a quartic whose Jacobian is D12/MW5, closing H3-03 at equation level.

events.behavior: The D12-to-A11 orbit42 profile, physical I8* marking, and eighteen identity-class zero-pole sections were recovered; fast point transport and rational-halving shortcuts were rejected.

events.behavior: The historical q8/orbit922 divisor was recognized as O+P-2F with zero vertical-root correction and transported through the complete root/MW/glue marking. The equation-side nef targets collapsed to orbits 12 and 2162, and orbit12 was selected by a declared minimum-MW-L1 convention.

events.status: exact partial target certificate plus bounded modular benchmark

events.behavior: The eighteen exact identity-shell points were found to span an index-five sublattice of the saturated rank-five MW hyperplane. The previously proposed pole-order-four missing direction lay in the wrong coset, while exhaustive exact enumeration selected the minimum-pole bridge M=(1,0,0,0,0,1) and the literal word P12=M+S6-2*S2-2*S8.
events.method: Compute the exact shell Smith index, enumerate all MW vectors through the pole-order-five height bound, filter by the transported target coset, verify the group-law coordinate identity, and compile a free-infinity finite-field chart for the bridge rather than a fixed leading branch.
events.meaning: The construction fingerprint extends beyond the target orbit to a precise quotient-lattice coset. The open symbolic solve drops from pole order six to pole order five without changing the marked target.
events.generalization: After transporting a historical divisor, compute the saturation quotient generated by known equation sections and solve in the target coset; a generic missing-rank generator may be both cheaper and irrelevant.
events.status: exact target-coset theorem plus bounded modular benchmark

events.behavior: Exact Mobius/quartic transport added the degree-one spinor curve to the two identity curves, but the unimodular D12-to-A11 transition proved that all twenty zero-pole classes have zero in the parent coordinate which becomes the sixth A11 MW coordinate. The alternative construction-compatible q8 orbit only reverses that missing coordinate.

events.meaning: The spinor and alternate-orbit shortcuts cannot construct the missing A11 direction; the smallest primitive parent carrier is the D12 P.O=4 vector (0,0,0,0,1), while the selected child bridge remains M=(1,0,0,0,0,1) with P.O=5.
events.generalization: Before launching elimination for a missing MW direction, compute the exact quotient-coordinate map on the full ambient basis and test every already-explicit curve and construction-equivalent marking. Once those alternatives are excluded, prefer resolved linear Riemann--Roch over a large generic section Groebner system.
events.status: exact construction aid and shortcut rejection

events.behavior: A proposed degree-five close_P24 carrier was obtained by composing coordinates in the A0-zero D12 frame with the orbit64 transition belonging to the distinct R3-zero frame. The associated modular composition did correctly expose a cancelled q24 base-locus branch, but the degree-five marking claim was invalid.

Among forty stored explicit classes the first positive carrier subset uses degrees 40 and 44. Low-cost lateral orbits 849 and 591 fail full nefness; passing candidates change the ADE route or lack a pinned continuation. The fixed-infinity bridge benchmark has 16 variables and 18 equations but full recurrence substitution raises degree to 36.

events.meaning: Keep the certified orbit12 route and replace the false quintic shortcut and large generic solve by a split-I12 norm/resolved-RR construction with bidirectional coefficient recurrences.

Over GF(131), fibrewise 7-by-8 Abel kernels interpolate an exact q4/orbit164 section with x degrees 32/28 and actual y degrees 47/42 inside the predicted numerator bound 48, from 122 good fibres.

Simultaneous projective reconstruction recovers exact compact QQ(t) coordinates of degrees 12/8 and 18/12; the primitive x and y vectors have maxima 363 and 526 bits, and fourfold pole growth gives canonical height 11.

events.behavior: Complete polynomial P.O=0 shells at four good primes did not realize the nominal Q1 branch. mechanisms.name: Shioda-Tate rank exchange
mechanisms.symptom: MW ranks appear or disappear under a neighbor.
mechanisms.resolution: Hold NS and rho fixed and verify delta(root_rank)+delta(mw_rank)=0.
mechanisms.meaning: Sections and reducible-fibre components are two presentations of the same divisor budget.
mechanisms.generalization: Use root rank as a controllable storage channel for MW rank when navigating fibrations.

mechanisms.name: Weyl fixed-component cancellation
mechanisms.symptom: A primitive isotropic class has negative intersections or large raw old-fibre degree.
mechanisms.resolution: Reflect in supplied effective (-2)-curves until the movable nef representative is reached; retain the removed fixed component sequence.
mechanisms.meaning: The divisor class is unchanged up to the Weyl action, while its effective presentation becomes a fibration pencil.
mechanisms.generalization: Make chamber reduction a first-class, replayable operation and never infer nefness from root type alone.

mechanisms.name: NS glue saturation
mechanisms.symptom: A computed MW regulator differs from the discriminant prediction by a perfect square.
mechanisms.resolution: Saturate trivial lattice plus section classes inside NS and project all glue cosets.
mechanisms.meaning: The missing classes are finite-index glue, not new analytic sections.
mechanisms.generalization: Record Smith invariants and torsion/glue before reporting an MW height lattice.

mechanisms.name: Cover-degree normalization
mechanisms.symptom: Heights and collision degrees are multiplied by four.
mechanisms.resolution: Account for the degree-two binary-quartic covariant map before applying the elliptic group law.
mechanisms.meaning: The transported point was 2P rather than P.
mechanisms.generalization: Annotate every point map with isogeny/cover degree and test it by canonical heights.

mechanisms.name: Full-denominator pole cancellation
mechanisms.symptom: A supposedly regular CRT frame retains a high-degree vertical pole.
mechanisms.resolution: Clear Nx/Dx and Ny/Dy completely; the q8 residue is Ny*Dx/(h*Dy), not Ny/(h*Dy).
mechanisms.meaning: A missing denominator factor changed the line bundle being compiled.
mechanisms.generalization: Derive local residues symbolically before modular normalization and regression-test generic branch degree.

mechanisms.name: Resolved-module saturation
mechanisms.symptom: Independent component rows overconstrain an RR pencil or raw minors share a spurious factor.
mechanisms.resolution: Use the saturated pushforward module and connected ADE quotient lines on physical resolved components.
mechanisms.meaning: Exceptional conditions have syzygies and cancellations dictated by the resolution graph.
mechanisms.generalization: Compile valuation modules and quotient conditions, not a row-per-centre heuristic.

mechanisms.name: Specialization rank and pole change
mechanisms.symptom: Generic P.O, MW coordinates, roots, or rank do not survive at CM24.
mechanisms.resolution: Transport the divisor, specialize, re-chamber, and recompute Picard rank, roots, heights, poles, and vertical support.
mechanisms.meaning: Extra algebraic classes can move rank between roots and sections; a specialized section label need not define the generic divisor.
mechanisms.generalization: Treat specialization as a new typed stage linked by a specialization map, never as an in-place coefficient substitution.

mechanisms.name: Marking-preserving transport
mechanisms.symptom: Two frames have the same ADE/MW label but lead to different endpoints or enormous pullback degree.
mechanisms.resolution: Retain the embedded U, zero, fibre, components, marked horizontals, and determinant-one NS transport in both directions.
mechanisms.meaning: An NS isometry may change the elliptic fibration; ADE/MW labels are not object identifiers.
mechanisms.generalization: Use marked-fibration nodes and lossless transport matrices as the graph state.

mechanisms.name: Numerical collision false rank
mechanisms.symptom: A tiny residual suggests a new section but its x-coordinate approaches an existing section and target/non-target incidence errors are comparable.
mechanisms.resolution: Require scale-free separation, edge-gap and wrong-sign-gap tests before promoting numerical rank growth.
mechanisms.meaning: Near-collision can mimic an independent MW direction.
mechanisms.generalization: Rank discovery needs independence/collision guards before exact lifting.

mechanisms.name: Collision-factor saturation
mechanisms.symptom: Repeated factors arise from normalized fibres or lambda=mu instead of distinct reducible fibres.
mechanisms.resolution: Saturate known boundary/collision factors and demand squarefree residual factors before lifting.
mechanisms.meaning: Raw gcd degree can count a degenerate collision locus rather than the desired Kodaira configuration.
mechanisms.generalization: Classify and remove geometric boundary factors before interpreting finite-field hits.

mechanisms.name: Construction-fingerprint transport
mechanisms.symptom: Many low-q neighbors have the same ADE child and local component profile, while a generic section solve is prohibitively large.
mechanisms.resolution: Recover the historical divisor formula and vertical support, split the marking isometry into root and MW blocks, enforce integral glue, match the transported divisor literally against the equation-side chamber search, and compute its coset modulo the saturated lattice generated by known equation sections.
mechanisms.meaning: The way a divisor was assembled can identify its equation-side orbit and the exact quotient-lattice coset that must be solved, even when ADE and q cannot.
mechanisms.generalization: Always audit the construction before launching symbolic elimination; preserve O/P/F coefficients, vertical-root support, root orientation, MW coordinates, full glue transport and the shell saturation quotient as first-class fingerprints.

mechanisms.name: Equation-effective zero gate
mechanisms.symptom: A low-cost marked suffix is lattice-valid but its proposed zero has negative intersection or differs from the rational curve used by the equation.
mechanisms.resolution: Identify the actual equation-side zero, reduce against the complete physical chamber, and recompute all next-divisor intersections and scores.
mechanisms.meaning: A chamber pseudo-zero can preserve an abstract lattice transport while invalidating the claimed equation continuation.
mechanisms.generalization: Do not promote continuation or cost claims until the zero is both effective and explicitly pointed on the current equation.

mechanisms.name: Branch-value interpolation
mechanisms.symptom: A resolved RR computation appears nonlinear although the selected horizontal has rational double-branch values on known fibres.
mechanisms.resolution: Interpolate the branch line and divide by the product of branch parameters before simplifying the denominator square.
mechanisms.meaning: The two-dimensional pencil can be recovered by linear interpolation rather than a generic Groebner solve.
mechanisms.generalization: Search for rational branch values, recurrence structure, and forced denominator squares before nonlinear elimination.

mechanisms.name: Layered endpoint certification
mechanisms.symptom: An exact lattice path to a known endpoint is mistaken for an equation or Mordell--Weil rank certificate.
mechanisms.resolution: Track marked route, characteristic-zero equations, endpoint sections/heights/saturation, Picard upper bound, and source identity as separate gates.
mechanisms.meaning: A terminal lattice isometry proves navigation data, not the existence and exact rank of sections on an explicit Weierstrass model.
mechanisms.generalization: Advance each proof layer independently and state the first unmet gate as the active frontier.

mechanisms.name: Resolved component versus node fingerprint
mechanisms.symptom: A section specializes to a singular Weierstrass node and a coarse component label gives a canonical height inconsistent with pole growth.
mechanisms.resolution: Multiply by the exponent of all component groups, recover heights from compact pole degrees, polarize the Gram, and use a local resolved chart to recover any oriented I_n label still needed.
mechanisms.meaning: The unresolved node forgets tangent-branch data and can identify several distinct resolved components.
mechanisms.generalization: Treat raw node incidence as a search fingerprint, never as a marked component certificate; audit heights independently before lattice embedding.

mechanisms.name: Projective rational-function reconstruction
mechanisms.symptom: Coefficientwise rational reconstruction keeps failing even after many good primes because monic polynomial normalization introduces a large common denominator.
mechanisms.resolution: CRT the full normalized coefficient vector, recover one primitive projective vector by a small integer-lattice reduction, and accept it only after exact equation substitution and reduction to every prime.
mechanisms.meaning: The rational function is intrinsically projective; reconstructing its shared scale once avoids paying separate numerator/denominator bounds for every coefficient.
mechanisms.generalization: For exact modular lifts of rational functions, try simultaneous projective reconstruction before enlarging the CRT modulus or lifting a larger auxiliary object.

mechanisms.name: Minimum-cost U before equation compilation
mechanisms.symptom: A known target frame is represented only by a huge transported fibre class, making direct equation recovery appear intrinsically expensive.
mechanisms.resolution: Enumerate and classify low-incidence primitive U embeddings on the simplest known equation, choose a shared-zero minimum-cost representative, and only then apply the classical neighbor linear system.
mechanisms.meaning: Equation size depends strongly on the marked copy of the fibration, not just its J2 frame class; a giant historical representative need not measure intrinsic accessibility.
mechanisms.generalization: Run inverse lattice discovery and incidence minimization before symbolic compilation, then recover endpoint sections from source curves meeting the selected fibre once.

mechanisms.name: Predictor versus target-fitted visibility
mechanisms.symptom: A low-genus pencil explains known exceptional directions only after those directions were used to fit the pencil.
mechanisms.resolution: Label it post-hoc visibility, freeze a predictor independently, and test the predictor on held-out exact controls before using it to order new candidates.
mechanisms.meaning: Existence of a target-conditioned incidence construction says nothing about prospective recall and cannot justify discarding unseen directions.
mechanisms.generalization: Separate explanation, ranking, and exhaustive exclusion in both data and theorem wording.

mechanisms.name: Arithmetic full-marking gate
mechanisms.symptom: A geometric Picard-rank-19 lattice and rootless MW17 frame appear to provide an arithmetic rank-17 fibration over QQ.
mechanisms.resolution: Compute the Galois action on the trivial lattice, MW lattice, and discriminant glue; require all nineteen named divisor classes and a saturated rational section basis over the base field.
mechanisms.meaning: Geometric Shioda--Tate rank need not survive as rational Mordell--Weil rank, and a geometric same-NS corridor cannot repair a missing rational source marking.
mechanisms.generalization: Make field-of-definition data part of every foundry state and fail before equation compilation when the full arithmetic marking is obstructed.

mechanisms.name: Formal branch versus algebraic rational source
mechanisms.symptom: A smooth modular point or long Hensel lift is treated as evidence that a rational characteristic-zero source equation exists.
mechanisms.resolution: Use a unit Jacobian minor to certify only the formal local branch, then require a separate algebraization or rational parametrization, a QQ-point, Picard-rank control, and the full rational NS marking.
mechanisms.meaning: Formal smoothness guarantees compatible local deformations, not global algebraicity or rationality.
mechanisms.generalization: Type finite-field, finite p-adic, formal, algebraic, and rational stages separately and never infer a later stage from an earlier one.

mechanisms.name: Finite quotient class slicing
mechanisms.symptom: A large unsliced polynomial system for a product-twist section is intractable, and one completed trace range is mistaken for all possible divisibility classes.
mechanisms.resolution: Derive the exact invariant/anti-invariant quotient, enumerate minimum-norm trace representatives, and solve one certified projective system per remaining quotient class.
mechanisms.meaning: The quotient can make the search finite and exact, but excluding its zero class does not exclude nonzero classes or prove rank zero.
mechanisms.generalization: Use exact cohomological or discriminant quotients to partition nonlinear searches, and state the surviving classes explicitly.

mechanisms.name: Coverage-certified sharded exhaustion
mechanisms.symptom: Many independently successful search chunks can still leave gaps, overlaps, exceptional traces, or silently missing output.
mechanisms.resolution: Declare half-open key ranges, validate every chunk schema and source hash, account separately for exceptional exact traces, and make the merger prove unique full-domain coverage before reporting a negative theorem.
mechanisms.meaning: The mathematical conclusion belongs to the coverage certificate, not to the fact that individual workers returned no hit.
mechanisms.generalization: Every distributed negative search needs an exact domain cardinality, gap/overlap checks, fail-closed parsing, and a compact merged certificate.

mechanisms.name: Mutable public source projection
mechanisms.symptom: A checker pins the hash of a live public database URL, but the upstream database grows and the historical bytes are no longer retrievable from that URL.
mechanisms.resolution: Preserve the exact claim-relevant records as a minimal repository projection with its own hash and source count; treat each later live fetch as a new snapshot instead of overwriting the old certificate.
mechanisms.meaning: A source hash detects drift but does not preserve replayability unless the referenced bytes or a sufficient exact projection are retained.
mechanisms.generalization: For mutable external datasets, store the smallest legally and scientifically sufficient snapshot needed to replay every claim, including null fields and selection rules.
